papers.title: There is no cubic 8-circulant nut graph: completing the existence classification of cubic polycirculant nut graphs
papers.scope: Bašić and Damnjanović, On cubic polycirculant nut graphs, arXiv:2411.16904v1 Conjecture 16 = Conjecture 1 of the published version (Comput. Appl. Math. 2025). Their Theorem 2 excludes l in {1,2,4,5} and constructs cubic l-circulant nut graphs for l in {3,6,7} and l >= 9; l = 8 was the only open case. Proof: a single kernel character on semiregular orbit coordinates gives a symmetric signed integral 8x8 quotient with nullity exactly one (injective lift) and nonzero diagonal cofactors; cubicity forces a local grammar; an inductive kernel-checked catalogue of 194 connected subcubic supports with 1,722 isomorphism certificates, 669 augmentations and tree switching reduce to 9,172 signed matrices, each excluded by an exact determinant (8,208) or zero principal cofactor (964) certificate. Valid for all orbit sizes m, without bounding graph order.

papers.title: Power-domination TAR uniqueness for complete bipartite graphs: PD^TAR(K_{s,t}) is unique if and only if s ≠ 2 and t ≠ 2
papers.scope: Bjorkman, Bozeman, Ferrero, Flagg, Grood, Hogben, Jacob and Reinhart, Power domination reconfiguration, arXiv:2201.01798, La Matematica 5 (2026): the uniqueness conjecture stated after Proposition p:K33 (still listed open in the Curtis-Flagg-Hogben survey arXiv:2406.05509v2, 2025). Proved: the new Core Theorem (for s,t >= 3, (s,t) != (3,3), K_{A,B} is the only graph on A ⊔ B with exactly its PD sets) via fort duality, pair forts, cross-degree rigidity isolating (3,3), two-sided completeness and independence; with the published TAR relabelling reduction (Bong-Carlson-Curtis-Haas-Hogben, Graphs Combin. 2023) formalized by a self-contained Hamming-isometry proof, and the source's small cases (K_2, K_{1,t}, K_{2,t} via K_{2,t}(e), K_{1,2} vs K_3, K_{3,3}) all formalized.

papers.title: Valuation differences for coloured binary partitions: the full Ulas–Żmija Conjecture 6.1 picture (even formula, odd bounds, sharpness, and failure of per-colour sharpness for m ≡ 15 mod 16)
papers.scope: Ulas and Żmija, arXiv:1904.03398v1 (Ramanujan J. 55 (2021) 623–660), Conjecture 6.1 on ν2(c_m(4n) − c_m(n)) for m-coloured binary partitions. Proved in full: the even formula ν2 = ν2(n) + 2ν2(k) + 3 for m = 2k; the bounds +3 (m ≡ 1 mod 4) and +6 (m ≡ 3 mod 4) with nonzero differences; explicit infinite equality families for m ≡ 1 (mod 4) and m ≡ 3, 7, 11 (mod 16); and for m ≡ 15 (mod 16) the universal +7 bound, so equality never holds. Hence the conjecture is false under the per-k reading and true under the some-k reading.

papers.title: An eight-vertex counterexample to the Li–Weng rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture (Conjecture 6.12 of arXiv:2004.06285v2)
papers.scope: Li and Weng, Further results on the rainbow vertex-disconnection of graphs, arXiv:2004.06285v2 Conjecture 6.12 (5.12 in v1; Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. 44 (2021)): rvd(G) + rvd(Ḡ) ≥ n for connected G, Ḡ of order n ≥ 8. False: an explicit connected 8-vertex graph G (masks 202,225,232,149,232,22,23,31) with connected complement has rvd(G) = 4 and rvd(Ḡ) = 3, sum 7. Supporting evidence: 74 of the 9,888 eligible order-8 isomorphism classes fail, and three connected one-vertex extensions fail at order 9 (sum 8 < 9), so the threshold is not merely off by one.

papers.scope: Jeffries-Yeats Conjecture 5.1 for doubled 3-regular graphs.
